placements.why: This envelope's entire content — a database adoption, its performance rationale, and its migration schedule — is an infrastructure/system-design decision. No strata exist yet in this repo; nothing in the supplied (empty) strata or narrative structure covers organizational-technology decisions, so the top-level bucket for this content must be minted fresh. 'Architecture' is the standard name for this category in the org's taxonomy and nothing existing is even close, so this is a NEW-tier mint with no parent required.
placements.title: Technical infrastructure and system-design decisions
placements.frame: What system, platform, or infrastructure choice is being made, and what technical rationale grounds it?

placements.title: Organizational commitment to adopt and migrate infrastructure
placements.frame: What infrastructure or system is being ratified as the settled choice, and what schedule commitment does the decision carry?
placements.why: src-1/src-4 ratify the Zypherion choice itself and src-3/src-6 ratify the migration schedule — both spoken and notetaker renderings of the same binding organizational determination (conviction reads mark all four 'decision'; relational reads mark all four authority-ranking). This names a recurring subject — infrastructure decisions and their accompanying rollout commitments — that future envelopes about other technology adoptions and their timelines will keep feeding, distinct from the one-time fact of Zypherion specifically. No existing leaf or strata sub-area covers this yet, and nothing supplied is close enough to warrant an INSPIRED lineage, so this is a NEW mint under the freshly minted Architecture strata.

placements.title: Technology choices justified by quantified performance gains
placements.frame: What quantified performance metric is offered as evidence for a technology or architecture decision, and against what baseline is it measured?
placements.why: src-2 and src-5 both state the same 15x columnar-query metric as the evidentiary basis for the adoption — once spoken, once in the notetaker's compressed catalog form — and conviction/relational reads mark both as 'claim'/market-pricing rather than 'decision'/authority-ranking, distinguishing them from the ratifying commitments above. This names a recurring pattern — quantified performance comparisons used to justify architecture decisions — that future envelopes evaluating other tools will keep feeding, not a one-time statistic itself (per the grain test, the 15x figure is evidence for this theme, not a leaf of its own). Nothing existing covers this and nothing is close enough for an INSPIRED lineage, so it mints standalone under Architecture, as a sibling to the adoption-commitments leaf.
